availability_provenance.note: Recorded 8 October 2026 for #377. The API states no publication time and keeps no vintages (it serves the current table), so the instant is Treasury's published schedule, not a measured one, and it is NOT VERIFIED from this environment: fiscaldata.treasury.gov (the dataset page that states the schedule) is refused by the proxy, and only the api. host is reachable. The schedule used is that the Daily Treasury Statement for a business day is published at 4:00 PM ET on the next business day. 16:30 ET is declared, 30 minutes after it and the same margin the bill-rate declaration takes over its bulk file's time, so a decision at 16:00 ET on that next business day does not read it and the first decision that does is the one after. The series' meaning and units were checked against FRED's WTREGEN (the H.4.1's weekly average of the TGA): the 7-calendar-day average of the daily closing balances ending each Wednesday, carried across weekends and holidays, matches WTREGEN to within 0.0009 USD billions on every one of the 451 Wednesdays 2018-01-17 to 2026-09-02 (tests/fixtures/snapshots/dts_inputs against funding_inputs/fred-macro-latest-vintage), which also settles that the line named 'Federal Reserve Account', 'Treasury General Account (TGA)' and 'Treasury General Account (TGA) Closing Balance' are one series across the renames. Units: the statement reports USD millions; the adapter divides by 1000.
availability_provenance.publication: Daily Treasury Statement (Bureau of the Fiscal Service), Table I, Operating Cash Balance, served as Fiscal Data's accounting/dts/operating_cash_balance table; published at 4:00 PM ET on the business day after the date it describes.

coverage: Treasury General Account closing balance, daily, 2018-01-02 onwards in the tracked snapshots (the table runs from 2005-10-03)
treasury_dts_tga.limitation: Off in every published declaration (#377), and declared here and not in metadata/sources.json, which the final-test pre-registration freezes by its bytes (docs/decisions/final-test-preregistration.md, amendment of 7 October 2026): the TGA the published declarations read is FRED's weekly WTREGEN (fred_macro_latest_vintage), and this daily series is read only by the measurement fields tga_daily, tga_daily_change and tga_change_x_reserves (repo_model.measurement_fields). The closing-balance line has had three names (the Federal Reserve Account, the Treasury General Account (TGA), and from the April 2022 redesign the Treasury General Account (TGA) Closing Balance, whose value sits in the open_today_bal column); the adapter reads each in its own column and refuses a date with two closing balances. Each snapshot is one unmodified, year-wide response; a re-fetch can differ.
treasury_dts_tga.provider: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Bureau of the Fiscal Service

release_lag.note: Declared 8 October 2026 (#377). The statement for a business day is published at 4:00 PM ET on the next business day (availability_provenance); 16:30 ET that day is declared, so the 16:00 ET decision of that day does not read it. The API states no publication time and keeps no vintages.

treasury_dts_tga.reviewed_note: Structural-zero semantics have not been reviewed against the Fiscal Data schema; the empty declaration is not a finding.

availability_provenance.note: Recorded 8 October 2026 for #377. Two business days after the reference date at 16:00 ET is the conservative availability instant declared here, as #187 directs when the publication time cannot be established; a one-business-day reading is reported as a sensitivity only.

ofr_stfm_repo_segments.limitation: Off in every published declaration (#377). A separate source from ofr_stfm_repo only so that metadata/sources.json, which the final-test pre-registration freezes by its bytes (docs/decisions/final-test-preregistration.md, amendment of 7 October 2026), is not edited. release_lag.note: Copied from ofr_stfm_repo.release_lag (#187), the same publication: Conservative, under docs/decisions/information-set.md (#187): the API states no publication time and keeps no vintages, and its one timestamp is a last-write time, so a day's value is declared available at 16:00 ET two business days after it. Values dated before 2020-09-09 were filled in after the OFR began publishing in real time, and are not read by the scored column.

ofr_stfm_repo_segments.reviewed_note: Structural-zero semantics have not been reviewed against the OFR API's schema; the empty declaration is not a finding. A null value is the OFR's own missing day.

availability_provenance.note: Recorded 8 October 2026 for #426. The columns are computed per panel row by repo_model.net_settlement from Fiscal Data's auctions_query records (tests/fixtures/snapshots/net_settlement_inputs/treasury_auctions, fetched 2026-10-08 with ingest.fetch_treasury_auctions), each auction counted from its announcemt_date. The dataset states no announcement clock time. Treasury's usual announcement time, 11:00 a.m. ET, is from general knowledge and was NOT verified from this environment; 12:00 ET is declared, an hour later, so a 16:00 ET decision of the announcement day reads the announcement and no decision before it does. The earliest closing of any auction in the snapshot is 10:00 a.m. (cash management bills announced and held on one day).
availability_provenance.publication: U.S. Treasury auction announcements (offering amount, and the estimate of the publicly held securities maturing on the settlement date), announced days before the auction and the settlement.

coverage: offering amounts and the publicly held maturing estimate of every Treasury auction settling 2018-01-02 to 2026-01-15 in the tracked snapshot
treasury_auction_net_settlement.limitation: Off in every published declaration (#426), and declared here and not in metadata/sources.json, which the final-test pre-registration freezes by its bytes (docs/decisions/final-test-preregistration.md): the published treasury_auctions source is dated from the settlement and its scheduled availability. These columns are read only by a track that switches them on (repo_model.net_settlement.COLUMN_FIELDS). The maturing figure is the announced estimate of the publicly held maturing amount by security type; a group of auctions announced with no figure (mostly cash management bills) reads zero maturing, so its net is its offering. A day partly announced reads low. SOMA add-ons are not in the net (they cancel against the SOMA's own maturing holdings).
treasury_auction_net_settlement.provider: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Bureau of the Fiscal Service

release_lag.note: Declared 8 October 2026 (#426). The value on the row of day t counts the auctions announced on or before t, at 12:00 ET on t (availability_provenance), so the 16:00 ET decision of t reads it. The announcement clock time is declared conservatively, not verified.

treasury_auction_net_settlement.reviewed_note: Structural-zero semantics have not been reviewed against the Fiscal Data schema; the empty declaration is not a finding.

availability_provenance.note: Recorded 8 October 2026 for #412. Not a fetched series: repo_model.policy_features computes each column per panel row from the point-in-time register metadata/policy_events.json (#376), reading only entries whose announcement instant is at or before 16:00 America/New_York on the row's own date. A source that states no release time is public from 23:59:59 on its date, so a 16:00 decision that day never sees it (docs/decisions/policy-point-in-time.md). 16:00 is the published records' decision time; a run at an earlier decision time is refused by the availability guard rather than read late.
availability_provenance.publication: metadata/policy_events.json, one entry per policy or legislative change with its announcement date and time and a primary source URL (Board of Governors press releases and implementation notes, Federal Reserve Bank of New York statements, congress.gov); tests/test_policy_features.py perturbs every entry announced after a decision instant and requires the columns at that instant unchanged.

coverage: policy and legislation register, one value per panel day, 2018-04 onwards
policy_register.limitation: Off in every published declaration (#412), and declared here and not in metadata/sources.json, which the final-test pre-registration freezes by its bytes (docs/decisions/final-test-preregistration.md, amendment of 7 October 2026). Not a panel column and not fetched: repo_model.policy_features computes the columns from the register and a track adds them to a scratch panel (scripts/policy_features.py). Entries whose source was not read when the register was built are flagged read_at_source false in the register.
policy_register.provider: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System; Federal Reserve Bank of New York; U.S. Congress

release_lag.note: Declared 8 October 2026 (#412). The value for a row is computed from entries announced at or before 16:00 ET on that row's own date, so it is public at that instant by construction and the 16:00 ET decision of that day reads it; the decision instant is the same row's, never a later one.

policy_register.reviewed_note: No structural zeros: a 0.0 is a computed value (no such policy in force), not a missing one.

availability_provenance.note: Recorded 9 October 2026 for #445, from the tracked snapshots of the Desk's operation results (tests/fixtures/snapshots/on_rrp_inputs/nyfed_on_rrp, the same records nyfed_on_rrp reads). The Desk states no publication clock time (nyfed_on_rrp.availability_provenance). The evidence is each record's lastUpdated, the time the Desk last wrote it: a record whose lastUpdated is on its own operation date is public no later than that time, because it cannot be written later than it was first written. Over the 1997 operation dates 2018-01-02 to 2025-12-31 that carry a reverse-repo operation, 1985 have every record last written on the operation date at or before 15:00 New York time (earliest 13:15:20, median 13:15:52, 99th percentile 13:22:17, latest 14:43:00 on 2023-07-17, an operation delayed to close at 14:00). The other 12 are not provable and are excluded, so the column is empty on them: 10 were written again on a later date (2018-03-29, 2018-12-04, 2019-04-18, 2020-04-09, 2020-07-02, 2021-04-01, 2021-09-03, 2021-09-10, 2022-11-17, 2023-01-05), where lastUpdated says nothing about the first write, and 2 were last written on their own date after 15:00 (2018-02-16 at 16:43:22, a record annotated that $14.050 billion less settled than was accepted, and the 2024-10-16 small-value exercise at 16:50:30) and are excluded because the time of their first write is not known. The reading assumes the Desk's API serves a record from the time it is written, which is not stated anywhere and cannot be verified from outside; a record could be written to the Desk's database before the API shows it. 15:00 is declared, 17 minutes after the latest included lastUpdated and an hour before the 16:00 decision. Note the exclusion looks at a record's later rewrites, which no forecast at the time could know; it only removes days, and whether a record was rewritten years later is unrelated to the spread.
availability_provenance.publication: New York Fed reverse repo operation results: the operation closes at 13:15 ET and the Desk's API carries the summary of results, last written at lastUpdated; 15:00 ET on the operation date is the declared availability instant for a day whose records were all last written on that date at or before 15:00.

coverage: overnight reverse repo amounts accepted on the operation date, for the dates whose evidence is proven
nyfed_on_rrp_sameday.limitation: Off in every published declaration (#445), and declared here and not in metadata/sources.json, which the final-test pre-registration freezes by its bytes. The same sum as nyfed_on_rrp (totalAmtAccepted over every Reverse Repo operation of the operationDate, USD billions) for a date whose evidence holds, and no value on any other date. The panel carries no value on a date without an operation (a federal holiday or a SIFMA full close).
nyfed_on_rrp_sameday.provider: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

release_lag.note: Declared 9 October 2026 (#445). The value for operation date d is declared public at 15:00 New York time on d, so the 16:00 decision of d reads it. Only dates whose records were all last written on d at or before 15:00 carry a value (availability_provenance). nyfed_on_rrp keeps its own conservative declaration (16:00 on the next business day), which this one does not replace.

nyfed_on_rrp_sameday.reviewed_note: Structural-zero semantics have not been reviewed against the operation-results schema; the empty declaration is not a finding.

availability_provenance.note: Recorded 9 October 2026 for #445. EXCLUDED: no publication time before 16:00 New York time can be established. Treasury's Daily Treasury Bill Rates page (tests/fixtures/snapshots/treasury_bill_rates_page, fetched 2026-10-09T03:02:41Z, sha256 949a9940...) states that the par yields are derived from indicative bid-side quotations 'obtained by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York at or near 3:30 PM each trading day' and states no time at which the rates are posted. The tracked yearly exports carry a retrieval time only (one fetch, 2026-09-14, or the commit time of the file) and the page keeps no vintages, so no archived copy dates a first posting; the page fetched here already carried the 8 October row when read, some 8 hours after the close. The Federal Reserve's H.15 file, which republishes the rates, is at 16:30 ET (treasury_bill_rates.availability_provenance). Quotes are struck at about 15:30, so a posting before 16:00 would leave under 30 minutes and nothing shows it happened. The input is therefore declared at the end of its own day, which no decision at 16:00 on the same day reads; it enters no nowcast and no forecast of this track.
availability_provenance.publication: Treasury Daily Treasury Bill Rates (home.treasury.gov): quotations obtained at or near 3:30 PM ET each trading day; no posting time stated.

coverage: bill rates by tenor, in percent, read on the day of the quotation
treasury_bill_rates_sameday.limitation: Declared so that the exclusion is a fact the as-of rule enforces: no column is built from it. A same-day reading of a bill rate is refused until a posting time before the decision is evidenced.

release_lag.note: Declared 9 October 2026 (#445): the end of the day of the quotation, the convention that asserts no earlier instant. The 16:00 decision of that day does not read it.

treasury_bill_rates_sameday.reviewed_note: Not a data input; nothing is read from this source.

availability_provenance.note: Recorded 9 October 2026 for #445. spread_nowcast_bps on the row of day r is computed by repo_model.nowcast from the spread of day r - 1 (SOFR is published at about 08:00 ET on r and declared public at 15:00 ET on r, nyfed_sofr.release_lag) and earlier days, the same-day reverse repo of r (nyfed_on_rrp_sameday, 15:00 on r), the gross Treasury settlement of r (treasury_auctions.scheduled_availability, 15:00 on the panel day before r) and the calendar. Its latest input is therefore public at 15:00 ET on r. Its ridge is fitted on pairs whose target row is at most r - 1. tests/test_nowcast.py checks both by changing every input from row r on, and every label from row r on, and asking the nowcast to stay the same.
availability_provenance.publication: Computed by this repository from the public inputs above; nothing is published.

coverage: a nowcast of the spread (SOFR - IORB, bp) of each panel day, made at 16:00 ET on that day
spread_nowcast.limitation: Off in every published declaration (#445). Read only by a track that switches the column on (repo_model.nowcast.COLUMN_FIELDS). It is the naive nowcast (the spread of day r - 1) wherever the model is not fitted or an input is missing. The constituents' timing is declared here, not through contract.FEATURE_FIELDS, because the as-of rule reads a derived feature at the latest row where every constituent is observable, which would put SOFR's lag on a value that is built for a day before SOFR is public.

release_lag.note: Declared 9 October 2026 (#445). The value on the row of day r is declared public at 15:00 ET on r, the latest of its inputs' instants, so the 16:00 decision of r reads it.

spread_nowcast.reviewed_note: Not a published source; the empty structural-zero declaration is not a finding.
